successors.name: Kingdom of Denmark
successors.text: the whole island, an integral part of the Kingdom of Denmark after 1953 ('In 1953, Greenland's colonial status was ended')

ledger.x: 1721: Hans Egede's Dano-Norwegian expedition begins the colonization of Greenland at Hope Colony on Kangeq.
1721: Greenland is a colony of Denmark-Norway.
1728: the royal colony is founded at Godthåb (Nuuk).
1734: the colony reaches Christianshåb (Qasigiannguit).
1738: Severin's monopoly trade reaches Jacobshavn and the Dutch are repulsed.
1741: Jacobshavn (Ilulissat) is founded.
1742: Frederikshåb (Paamiut) is founded.
1752: Claushavn is founded.
1754: Fiskenæs is founded.
1755: Ritenbenck, Egedesminde and Sukkertoppen are founded.
1756: Holstensborg (Sisimiut) is founded.
1758: Umanak (Uummannaq) is founded.
1769: the districts between the 1750s colonies are filled in (confidence 1).
1771: Upernavik is founded.
1773: Godhavn is founded on Disko Island.
1774: Julianehaab (Qaqortoq) is founded and the Royal Greenland Trade Department replaces the General Trade Company.
1788: Cliopatria adds 74 cells between 61.3N and 64.3N (confidence 1: bridging).
1797: Nennortalik, the last settlement for a century, is founded.
14 January 1814: the Treaty of Kiel leaves Greenland with Denmark when Norway is ceded; the colony passes from Denmark-Norway to the Kingdom of Denmark.
14 January 1814: the colony's metropole, the union of Denmark and Norway, ends.
14 January 1814: Greenland remains a Danish colony under the Kingdom of Denmark.
1894: a Danish trading station is founded at Ammassalik (Tasiilaq) on the east coast.
1908: four detached cells appear at the far north (confidence 1: bridging).
1910: Knud Rasmussen and Peter Freuchen set up a trading post at North Star Bay (Thule).
1917: the United States gives up its territorial claims in the Thule area.
1925: Ejnar Mikkelsen founds Scoresbysund (Ittoqqortoormiit) on the east coast.
June-July 1931: Norway occupies Erik the Red's Land on the east coast.
5 April 1933: the Permanent Court of International Justice rules against Norway and awards the east coast to Denmark.
1933: the east-coast zone passes to Denmark.
1936: the whole island is drawn as Greenland.
9 April 1940: with Denmark occupied by Germany, Greenland governs itself.
9 April 1940: Greenland's tie to occupied Denmark is cut.
9 April 1941: Greenland becomes a protected state of the United States.
1945: Danish rule from Copenhagen resumes and the American protection ends.
1945: Greenland is again a Danish colony ruled from Copenhagen.
1953: the colony's dependency on Denmark ends as Greenland becomes part of the Danish Realm.
1953: Greenland's colonial status ends and it becomes part of the Kingdom of Denmark.

wars.name: Battle of Jacobshavn
wars.outcome: The monopoly holder Jacob Severin 'successfully repulsed the Dutch at the Battle of Jacobshavn'; no change of land is recorded.

wars.name: Eastern Greenland case (Norwegian occupation of Erik the Red's Land)
wars.outcome: Norway occupied the east coast in 1931 and proclaimed it Norwegian on 10 July; the Permanent Court of International Justice ruled against Norway and awarded the disputed territory to Denmark (5 April 1933), after which Norway abandoned its claim.

wars.name: German weather stations on East Greenland (Second World War)
wars.outcome: The Germans set up four clandestine weather stations on the east coast from August 1942; the Sledge Patrol and American forces attacked or captured them (Holzauge found 11 March 1943, Bassgeiger attacked 22 April 1944, Edelweiss II captured 4 November 1944)…

certainty.note: A colony of settlements and trading districts along the south-west and west coast, later two spots on the east coast; no survey lines.
The island's coast is the frontier.
